summary.headline: Suryoday Q2 FY27: gross advances up 34.6% YoY to INR14,972 crores; gross NPA fell to 2.9% from 6.5% after INR596 crores write-offs and OTS.
summary.overview: Gross advances including IBPC reached INR14,972 crores (+34.6% YoY) and disbursements were INR3,096 crores (+27.4%). Net interest income rose 42.8% YoY to INR368.8 crores with NIM at 7.2%, and PAT was INR76.5 crores. Gross NPA dropped to 2.9% from 6.5% in June, helped by INR387 crores of CGFMU claims received in July and INR596 crores of write-offs and OTS. Management kept FY27 guidance of 30-35% advances growth and exit RoA of 1.4-1.5%, and reiterated PAT of about INR300 crores, while flagging drought exposure in Karnataka and Maharashtra and an unresolved CGFMU cover renewal.

financial_highlights.change: Tier 2 raise of INR200 crores added ~1.8%

segments.name: Inclusive finance (IF / MFI)
segments.commentary: Share of gross advances at about 41% (some reports cite 45%); current-bucket efficiency 99.3% vs 99.2% in Q1. Q2 slippages in IF about INR65 crores, up about INR20 crores QoQ.

segments.name: Retail assets
segments.commentary: About 59% of advances; mortgages and commercial vehicles (CV) growing 36% YoY. Management expects secular growth above 35% to continue in mortgages and CV.

segments.name: Digital / CLOU (credit line on UPI)
segments.commentary: CLOU portfolio about INR350 crores, expected INR500-600 crores by year-end; convenience fee income rose about INR14 crores QoQ. Over 14 lakh customers targeted; over 2 lakh onboarded via digital deposit channel.

segments.name: PSLC income
segments.commentary: About INR8 crores in Q2 vs about INR45 crores in Q1 (down about INR37 crores QoQ); guided to about INR5 crores in Q3.

guidance_outlook: FY27 advances growth guided at 30-35%; CFO says growth will be better than lower end of range.
Exit RoA guided at about 1.4-1.5%; PAT of about INR300 crores for FY27 reiterated, with guidance not revised upward.
Retail-to-IF mix of 45-55 kept as a medium-term target; management does not expect to reach it by year-end FY27.
Monthly IF disbursement run-rate of INR450-550 crores targeted over next 5 months as about 50 branches are added; October at INR450-475 crores.
FY28 guidance to be given with Q4 results; management expects at least mid-level of 30-35% growth to continue.
Tier 2 balance of INR200 crores targeted by December or by Q4 FY27; another CRAR uplift of 1.8-2% expected.
capex_capacity: About 50 new branches planned over the next 4-5 months; about 10 already opened, with contribution of INR50-60 lakhs per branch and about INR30 crores of disbursement expected from new branches by February.
CRAR at 19.37% in Q2, below the earlier 20-22% comfort range; management now cites 18.5-19% as comfort zone for CRAR and about 20% for Tier 1.
Tier 2 raise of INR200 crores in first week of October; a further INR200 crores (INR100 crores approved by board) to be raised, timing dependent on rate stabilisation.
NABARD variable-rate borrowing of INR1,200 crores taken at about 8.5%, now about 7.5%; treasury evaluating switch to fixed rate.
demand_pricing: Credit demand healthy system-wide; deposit mobilisation competitive with credit outpacing deposits. Management says funding costs are back in focus after the rate environment shifted.
Yield on advances rose about 60 bps QoQ; cost of funds down about 10 bps QoQ; NIM flat QoQ despite INR600 crores cash, due to lower PSLC income and excess liquidity.
Paying-book yield for Q2 was a little above 17.5% (Q1 cited 17.4%); MFI yield about 25.8%; management expects similar range for next two quarters.
Gross write-off of INR591 crores, almost entirely JLG and individual loans (IL) under CGFMU cover; retail write-off about INR3 crores.
Q2 disbursements into IF about INR450 crores per month; IBPC renewal expected at rates below 5% for six-month money.

qa_highlights.question: Is the CGFMU guarantee cover currently active, and what provision is being made for it?
qa_highlights.answer: Cover for FY27 disbursements has not opened as the central government must notify renewal; bank is providing about INR40-45 crores in H1 for premiums (about 1-1.5% fees, INR70-80 crores expected). Disbursements up to 31 March 2026 are fully covered and renewed.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure and collections in drought-hit districts?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,000-1,100 crores of exposure in affected Karnataka and Maharashtra areas, nearly all CGFMU-covered except about 3% (INR300-350 crores of last-six-month disbursements not yet covered). September and October collections stable; management expects a possible lagged impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 growth and the PAT guidance still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Advances growth guidance of 30-35% maintained; PAT of about INR300 crores still achievable, supported by the digital/CLOU business. Q2 PAT of INR76.5 crores is similar to Q1 despite lower PSLC income.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to NIM and cost-to-income going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM expected to be broadly stable with marginal improvement as MFI share rises; CTI of 70.5-70.6% reported, about 68.6% net of partner payouts. CGFMU cost shave-off not significant.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 slippage split, and what caused the rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 slippages of INR122 crores, about INR65 crores in IF and the rest in secured and digital; CV slips in a few accounts. Management views normal IF slippages at INR50-60 crores per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is there Tier 1 or capital optimisation planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is open to IBPC and fixed-rate NABARD refinancing; Tier 1 comfort zone cited as about 20%, moving to 18.5-19% for CRAR. Further Tier 2 raise planned before year-end.

risks_watch: CGFMU cover renewal: fresh-disbursement cover not yet open for FY27; if delayed, Q3 provisioning and P&L could be affected.
Drought in Karnataka and Maharashtra (Marathwada and south Karnataka): management expects possible lagged impact on collections in coming months; a tightening of micro-mortgage norms is planned.
Funding cost pressure: deposit mobilisation competitive, short-end rates volatile; Tier 2 raise timing uncertain.
CLOU credit quality: new product scaling to INR500-600 crores; management says one year of track record is needed before drawing conclusions.
IF share of advances at about 41% vs 45-55 retail/IF guidance; reaching target depends on IF growth outpacing retail.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality headline and PAT guidance, but cautious on drought and CGFMU timing; management repeatedly says it will wait and see and avoided upward guidance revisions.
key_quotes: We remain focused on the full-year objective of 30% to 35% advances growth and an exit ROA of approximately 1.4% to 1.5%, while continuing to assess developments in the operating environment.
Our bank is a clear market leader in the credit line on UPI, CLOU offering.

adds.what: About 50 new branches over next 4-5 months (about 10 already opened) for Inclusive Finance

growth.why: FY27 advances growth guided at 30-35% (CFO says better than lower end) and PAT ~INR300 crore held, backed partly by about 50 new branches (about 10 open) targeting INR450-550 crore monthly IF disbursements, plus CLOU growth to INR500-600 crore and mortgage/CV growth above 35%; flagged risks include drought exposure, CGFMU cover renewal, and PSLC income falling to about INR8 crore from INR45 crore.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM at 7.2% (+28 bps YoY) and management expects broadly stable NIM with marginal improvement as MFI share rises, but PSLC income fell to INR8 crores from INR45 crores in Q1 with guidance of about INR5 crores in Q3, and CGFMU premium provisioning of INR70-80 crores is a drag.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 50 new IF branches planned over 4-5 months with about 10 already opened, targeting monthly IF disbursements of INR450-550 crores over the next 5 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances grew 34.6% YoY to INR14,972 crores and FY27 growth guided at 30-35% (CFO says better than lower end), with disbursements up 27.4% to INR3,096 crores and CLOU expected to reach INR500-600 crores by year-end from INR350 crores.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No new capex discussed; CRAR fell to 19.37% (below earlier 20-22% comfort zone, now 18.5-19%) so further capital raises are planned (INR100 crores board-approved Tier 2, plus Tier 2 balance of INR200 crores by Dec or Q4 FY27), not physical capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management kept FY27 guidance of 30-35% growth, PAT of about INR300 crores and exit RoA of 1.4-1.5% and avoided upward revisions, with H1 PAT only about INR76.5 crores in Q2 (similar to Q1) despite lower PSLC income.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: CGFMU fresh-disbursement cover for FY27 not yet open (INR300-350 crores of last-six-month disbursements uncovered), drought exposure of INR1,000-1,100 crores in Karnataka/Maharashtra with possible lagged collection impact, and PSLC income falling to about INR5 crores in Q3; PAT of INR300 crores needs roughly INR224 crores more in H2 after INR76.5 crores in Q2.

rows.label: CLOU (credit line on UPI) scaling to INR500-600 crores
rows.why: CLOU portfolio about INR350 crores now, expected INR500-600 crores by year-end, with over 14 lakh customers targeted; management says one year of track record needed before drawing conclusions on credit quality.

rows.label: CGFMU cover renewal for FY27 disbursements
rows.why: Cover for FY27 disbursements has not opened as central government must notify renewal; bank provisioning about INR40-45 crores in H1 with INR70-80 crores expected for premiums (about 1-1.5% fees).

rows.label: NABARD fixed-rate switch
rows.why: NABARD variable-rate borrowing of INR1,200 crores taken at about 8.5%, now about 7.5%, and treasury is evaluating a switch to fixed rate for funding stability.

tone.note: Management was confident on advances growth, the 34.6% YoY loan growth, the GNPA fall to 2.9% and holding PAT of about INR300 crores, but cautious on drought exposure, CGFMU cover timing and CRAR; analysts probed CGFMU provisioning, drought-district collections, NIM and cost-to-income.
